capabilities.name: Multi-document ingestion with file-type checks, limits and hashing
capabilities.note: PDF, PNG and JPEG by their first bytes. By default 10 MB, 20 pages and 10 documents per case. Files are stored under their sha256; a rejected file becomes a limitation with a reason.

capabilities.name: Document classification
capabilities.note: Rules over words and layout. Three types have a spec at this build (bank statement, payslip, loan application), written for one drawn layout each; anything else is 'unknown' and says so. Wording that differs from the specs' may also read as 'unknown'. Held-out (eval/test.md): the type was recognised for all 440 documents, on both drawn layouts, digital and scanned; all of them are of the three supported types, so a fourth kind of document is not tested. A model never decides the type: with --llm a local model reads facts on pages whose type came out 'unknown' (the template-free row) and leaves the type as it is.

capabilities.name: Text-layer reading and OCR (offline)
capabilities.note: Every word has a box in page pixels. Scanned pages get a quality class from sharpness, not from the recogniser's score; numbers read from a degraded or poor page are flagged, not trusted. OCR output is a reading, not ground truth. A page that stands on its side (a scan or a PDF page turned a quarter turn) is read as poor and the dossier says why; a page turned half a turn is not recognised (limitation 36). Held-out (eval/test.md), on documents nobody changed: no amount, date or id was both wrong and trusted; 16 text values were.

capabilities.name: Structured extraction: fields and tables, each with a confidence and a location
capabilities.note: Bank statements, payslips and loan applications, digital and scanned (scans are simulated at three levels), on the drawn layouts the specs were written for. A column or label that is not found is reported as missing, never filled in, and nothing repairs a misread digit or separator. How many values come out right, wrong or missing, by kind of value and scan level, is measured by the evaluation, not by the tests (eval/test.md). Held-out, on documents nobody changed: layout A, which the specs were written for, is read right in every amount, date, id and text value on digital pages, and on mild scans in every amount, date and id and in 99.4 % of text values (4 of 625 wrong, and trusted); at 150 dpi 89.6 % of amounts are read and the rest are missing, and at 120 dpi 20.3 % are read (12 wrong, none trusted). Layout B was drawn after the specs were final, and about half of its labels, column headings and captions are wordings the specs do not list, so it is read much less: on digital pages 91 % of amounts, 97 % of dates and 34 % of text values, and no id. None of the values not read on those pages was wrong; each is reported missing. No amount, date or id was wrong and also trusted, in either layout; 16 text values were. A deduction beside an empty earnings cell is not read as a row. Other document types and layouts are not built by these specs; with --llm a local model reads some facts on pages of an unsupported type (next row).

capabilities.name: Template-free extraction: facts on pages of an unsupported type, read by the local model
capabilities.note: Optional, and off unless a run is started with --llm. A page whose type has no spec ('unknown') is shown to the local model (phi4-mini 3.8B through Ollama on this computer; the client refuses any other host) as numbered lines of text, at most 60 lines of the first 2 pages of a document. The model names the facts the page states, each with the words it took the value from; code then looks for those words among the page's word boxes, and an item whose words are not on the page, or whose value is not inside them, is dropped and logged (digits are never matched by similarity). The value kept is the page's own text with a box and a page; only the name is the model's. Every such field is marked as read by the model, has a confidence below the doubt limit, is labelled inference in the dossier and on the page, feeds no check and raises no finding, and the type is still decided by the rules. A call that fails, times out or cannot end inside the time budget is a limitation, and the model is not asked again for that case. Measured on ext-dev (docs/spike-x-extraction.md, eval/x/): 7 synthetic cases of an invoice and an electricity bill in two layouts, digital and scanned at three levels, with 182 printed facts written down before any model read a page. 97 facts were read at the right box under an acceptable name, 60 more by the rules alone, 8 partly (two fields joined into one), 1 under another name, 16 not read. It falls short on layout B (two labels on one line, their values on the next), on the tax amount of 2 of 7 invoices and on the 120 dpi bill (9 of its 15 facts missing). One run per model, on one machine, a page taking 60 to 123 s on this CPU; the held-out ext-test split was not read by any model. Partial: two synthetic layouts, no claim beyond these counts.

capabilities.name: Digital PDF forensics: comparison of saved revisions
capabilities.note: Text that differs between a PDF's earlier saved version and a later one is reported as an observation, with the old and the new text. Held-out: found and located in 8 of 8 incremental edits (D1), and raised on no genuine document. The other digital checks are in the next row.

capabilities.name: Digital PDF forensics: covered and hidden text, pictures over text, fonts, file metadata
capabilities.note: Reported as observations with the measured values: text still in the file but drawn under a filled rectangle or a picture that comes after it (the text written over a covering rectangle is cited too); a figure or date set in a different font, size or colour from the others in its column or on its line; text that is invisible, under 2 pt or off the page; a producer or creator that names PDF-editing software; a modification date later than the creation date. Held-out, 8 cases each, all found and (for D2, D3 and D5) located at the changed place: a cover with the text retyped in the same font (D2), the same in a near font (D3, a change the development set never showed), a metadata edit (D4) and a picture over text (D5); none of these checks raised a finding on a genuine document. Every case comes from one generator, and real editing software varies. Not built: text hidden by its colour, covers that are not rectangles, bold against regular.

capabilities.name: Scan and image forensics
capabilities.note: Two checks on scanned pages that are not of poor quality, both shown as observations: words whose image grain differs from the page median, and words set out of line after the page is straightened (a word against its row, a figure's right edge against its column, a figure's height against the page's other figures). Held-out (eval/test.md): of 16 scans changed by pasting from another scan (S1) or by erasing and retyping (S2), 6 were found and 10 missed. The placement check found 1 of the 8 pasted scans and the grain check 2 of the 8 retyped ones; the other finds came from arithmetic and cross-document checks. Counting every kind of change, 21 of 36 changes on scans were found (mild 13 of 18, 150 dpi 6 of 9, 120 dpi 2 of 9). One genuine 120 dpi scan was flagged by the placement check, the only flag on 144 genuine documents. A page read by OCR whose paper carries no scanner grain (a page printed or rendered to a picture) is not given to the grain, placement and learned-word checks; the document gets one limitation naming the page and saying so. The line is a grain share of 0.5 of the flat paper; the project's simulated scans measured 0.885 to 0.914 and noise-free pictures 0.004 to 0.153. No real scanner was measured: a real scan that is very clean, cut at white or denoised may be taken for such a page, and the dossier then says so.

capabilities.name: Compression history of a scanned picture (JPEG ghosts, error-level analysis over many qualities): places without the trace of the page's earlier save
capabilities.note: A scanned page that is a JPEG picture is saved again at qualities 25 to 95; where the page was saved earlier at a lower quality, the ink still carries that earlier save, and compact regions of ink that do not carry it are reported as one observation a page, with their boxes, the two qualities and the ordinary causes (a page put together from more than one scan; a stamp, date, page number or sticker that the scanner or a program added later). Development figures only (eval/e/): on the 36 synthetic payslip scans of the ext-dev pack, a pasted or retyped part with the last save at least 10 quality points above the earlier one was found at its place in 16 of 16 cases, with no region on 12 unchanged scans (of which 2 cannot be examined: last save under quality 40); on 72 further scans of the same generator, which set no constant, in 32 of 32 cases, with no region on 24 unchanged scans (of which 4 cannot be examined); and no region on the 90 scans of the dev split that nobody changed as a picture (of which 21 cannot be examined). The region stage, which draws the boxes, ran only on the resaved scans among them (6 of the 12, 12 of the 24, none of the 90): a scan saved once has no earlier save and is silent by design. Of the 8 ext-dev cases it cannot see by construction (an edit made with the page's own grid and quality, or a last save too close to the earlier one), a region touched the edge of the pasted box on 3 and sat at the edit on none. The project's own splice, a part of another scan of the same level pasted at the same place (the pack's aligned kind), is in that class: on the dev split a region appeared on 1 of its 5 scans (dev-0021; cause not examined, not claimed as a find) and on dev-0051 (120 dpi) the history was found and no region; the 16 of 16 and 32 of 32 come from a pack that pastes off the page's grid on purpose or types a new amount. With earlier saves written with Photoshop-family quantisation tables it found none of 18 edits; with earlier saves at qualities between the steps of 5 it found all 16 but named the earlier quality exactly on 0 of 16 (it names where the trace shows). A page saved once gives nothing. A picture that is not the saved JPEG (PNG, the rendered page of a scanned PDF, a scaled or turned picture) is a limitation, never a pass; scanned PDFs are not examined. Constants were set on the first 36 cases (in-sample); one generator and one JPEG writer; the held-out ext-test split was not run on this check. Partial: synthetic scans only, no claim beyond these counts.

capabilities.name: Learned word check on scanned pages: fourteen measures per word, weighted by a regression fitted to synthetic edits
capabilities.note: The one check that is fitted to data instead of written by hand. For each word of a scanned page that is read by OCR, is not of poor quality and is large enough to measure (a page with fewer than 12 measurable words is skipped, with a limitation), fourteen measures compare the word with the rest of its page: grain, edge sharpness, stroke width and share of ink, JPEG block edges at the page's grid and at other phases, baseline slope, the scores of the placement check, and how far the word sits off the line of the words beside it. A weighted sum of the standardised measures (logistic regression fitted in numpy, no new dependency, no random numbers; the weights are in learned_patches.json with the data they were fitted to and a hash of the label files) is the word's score. Words that reach a limit fixed on development data are listed, at most eight, in one visual observation per page, each with its box, its score and the three measures that raised it most. The score is not a probability and does not say that anything was changed. Fitted on 295 development cases (525 scan pages; 319 of 46,290 words lie inside an edit); the test and ext-test splits were not used, not even for the limit. The bar was written into evaluation/train_patches.py before the first fit and judged once, on cases held out from fitting: 16 of 36 pages with a part of another scan pasted in, against 3 for the grain and placement checks, and 59 of 72 pages of the compression-history pack, against 19; none of 195 unedited pages flagged, no region marked on one. The three existing scan checks together find 9 of 36 and 55 of 72 of those pages; this check finds 8 and 11 that none of the three finds, and misses 1 and 7 that they find. By kind on the held-out pack pages: pasted blocks 18 of 18, pasted fields 17 of 18, the same place of another payslip's scan pasted in 12 of 18, retyped amounts 12 of 18 (the grain and placement checks find 18 of 18). On parts of another scan pasted in, two hand-written measures of how far a word sits off its line carry most of the gain (alone 13 of 72 development pages; the other twelve alone none). The figures are by construction: generator, edits and check have one author, the weights were fitted to this generator's edits, and the scans are the simulator's (JPEG, three levels of quality); no real scan was used. Not looked at: digital documents, scans of poor quality, other file formats of a scan. A page read by OCR whose paper carries no scanner grain (a page printed or rendered to a picture) is not given to the grain, placement and learned-word checks; the document gets one limitation naming the page and saying so.

capabilities.name: Raw file structure: bytes after the end of a file or picture, /Info against XMP, signature range, embedded files and action keys, rebuilt index, editor named in picture metadata
capabilities.note: Facts read from the stored bytes of a PDF, JPEG or PNG, reported as observations that point at the whole document, each with a byte offset or object number and at most 32 bytes shown as hex and ASCII: bytes after the last end-of-file marker of a PDF, or after the end of a JPEG or PNG (also for the JPEG pictures inside a PDF, the first 50 of them); an /Info record that differs from the XMP packet in producer, creator tool or either date; a signature /ByteRange that stops short of the end of the file or runs past it; embedded files (name and size) and the names of the action keys /JavaScript, /JS, /OpenAction, /AA and /Launch, never opened or run; a PDF whose index had to be rebuilt to be read; an image-editor name in EXIF Software, XMP CreatorTool or PNG Software, and an EXIF save time later than the time taken. A signed PDF always gets a limitation, because the signature itself is not checked. Measured on 120 files built for the purpose by one generator (the structure pack of the repository's dataset generator, ext-dev): no observation on the 60 untouched files, all 80 expected observations on the 60 files with one planted change, none that was not expected. These figures are by construction: the same author wrote the pack and the check, and the changes were chosen with the check in view. They are not a detection rate and say nothing about files made by other programs. Every one of these facts also occurs in ordinary files (a second signature, a countersignature or a form filled in after a signature; a file saved again in place; padding or a trailer written by a program; an attachment or an /OpenAction written by a generator; an /Info record that differs from the XMP packet; an editor used to crop a genuine photograph), and anyone who can write a file can write each of these fields. Not built: bytes before the PDF header (an upload like that is turned away), file-attachment annotations, text chunks stored after the image data of a PNG, a JPEG picture inside a PDF with another filter in front of DCT, signature cryptography, malware detection.

capabilities.name: Cloned regions inside one page, and logos or stamps reused on two documents
capabilities.note: Not built. A region copied inside one page is not looked for, and a logo or stamp reused unchanged on two documents is not flagged (they are compared for difference, not for sameness). A first attempt to compare stamps for sameness was dropped: at its limit of 2 % it flagged 18 of the 48 separate synthetic stamp pressings (8 of the 24 genuine cases raised a false observation), and 27 of the 48 lie within the 5 % used for signatures, so no limit kept the copies and left the separate pressings alone (eval/h/reuse-ext-dev-stamps.md; the tool commit it names, 39f1b03, is 6f9c5b2 in the history after a rebase). A changed part of a scan is looked for only through the grain, placement and compression-history checks above. Photographs are out of scope.

capabilities.name: Signature comparison across documents
capabilities.note: The drawn signature on each document that has a signature caption in its spec (loan application, payslip) is cut out above that caption, straightened by the page's turn if it is a scan, and compared with the signature on every other such document by shape. A pair that differs by more than the stated limit is an inconsistency with both signatures marked; every pair compared is written to the audit trail. A signature that cannot be found or read (no ink, no caption, a poor page, printed matter in the area) is a limitation, never a pass. Shapes only: it does not say who signed. Held-out: a signature in another hand (C4) was found in 8 of 8 cases (4 digital and 4 scanned, one of them at 120 dpi), and the check raised no finding on a genuine document. The held-out signatures come from the same generator and the same invented names as the development ones, so other styles of signature are untested.

capabilities.name: A signature that is the same image on two documents of one case
capabilities.note: Two documents of one case that have a signature caption in their spec are compared for sameness: the two signatures are cut out, set on a 192 x 64 canvas and compared ink against ink, with a slide of 1 px and no turn. When at most 5 % of the ink of either signature lies more than 1 px from the other's ink, the pair is one observation with both signatures marked and the ordinary causes beside it (software that puts one stored image of a signature on every document it makes, one page submitted in two forms, one scan used for two documents). It does not say who signed. A mark that fills more than half of its canvas (a solid bar, a dot, a block) is not a stroke and is skipped, with a line in the audit trail; a mark that is not solid, such as a hollow box or a diagonal stroke, is compared, and one printed the same on two documents will be reported. The half is a plain line and not a measured boundary: a dashed rule, or a rule that is not quite level, can fall on either side of it. A 64-bit hash of each signature is written to the audit trail beside the gap and does not decide: 29 of 47 separate pairs lie within the 8 bits of the farthest copy. Development figures only (eval/h/reuse-ext-dev.md, 72 synthetic cases: 24 repeat a signature, 24 repeat a stamp, 24 are genuine); the limit was set on these pairs, so the figures are in-sample: 23 of 24 repeated signatures were found at their place (the miss is a 120 dpi scan whose copies lie 6.7 % apart), none of 47 pairs from separate signings was flagged (the nearest lies 8.8 % apart), and none of the 23 genuine cases in which a pair was compared raised an observation (in the other one no pair was compared: the caption of the signature was not found on one document of a 120 dpi scan, which the dossier lists as a limitation). The ink share of the 142 compared canvases lies between 0.089 and 0.185 (median 0.119), well under the half at which a mark is skipped. The held-out ext-test split was not run on this check. Stamps and logos are not looked at: a first attempt that compared stamps as well, at a limit of 2 %, flagged 18 of the 48 separate synthetic stamp pressings (8 of the 24 genuine cases raised a false observation), and 27 of the 48 lie within the 5 % used for signatures (eval/h/reuse-ext-dev-stamps.md; the tool commit it names, 39f1b03, is 6f9c5b2 in the history after a rebase), because the pressings the generator makes differ from one another by little more than the check can tell apart. Whether real stamps would separate is not known. A signature that was redrawn or traced is not reported. Partial: synthetic signatures from one generator, no claim beyond these counts.

capabilities.name: Checks within one document
capabilities.note: Bank statement balance chain and dates; payslip totals, net pay against its words, and pay date against pay month; the weekday printed on a loan application. Each states its tolerance. A conflict resting on a doubtful reading is shown as a possible extraction error. Held-out (eval/test.md): where a value these checks need is missing or unreadable they say so ('Cannot fully verify') and check no further. That happened for all 24 genuine statements and all 24 genuine payslips of layout B; for none of the 18 genuine cases of layout A that were digital or mild scans; and for the 6 genuine statements and 2 of the 6 genuine payslips of layout A scanned at 150 or 120 dpi.

capabilities.name: Cross-document conflict checks
capabilities.note: Name, address and employer across documents, graded as passing, written differently (observation), Minor mismatch or Mismatch; account number, which matches or is a Mismatch; net pay against the credits on a statement; declared income against gross earnings; the application date against the dates of the other documents; a file submitted twice; the same producing software on different kinds of document made minutes apart. A comparison that cannot be made is reported as a limitation, never as a pass. Built for three document types with one drawn layout each. Each finding prints its tolerance. Held-out (eval/test.md): a pay figure changed so that the payslip still adds up (C1) was found in 5 of 8 cases (0 of 3 where deductions were lowered), a name, address, employer or month changed in one document (C2) in 6 of 8, and a statement submitted twice (C3) in 8 of 8. The five misses left only limitations on the changed document: a comparison could not be made because a value was not read, or (a 120 dpi scan) a mismatch was shown as a possible extraction error to verify.

capabilities.name: Declared existing EMI against the instalments on a bank statement
capabilities.note: The existing EMI that a loan application declares, against the instalments that a bank statement shows being paid. A debit counts as an instalment when its narration holds the whole word EMI, instalment (or installment, instl) or loan and no word that makes it a fee, a reversal or a closing payment (fee, charge, penalty, GST, tax, bounce, return, refund, reversal, waiver, insurance, premium, closure, foreclosure, prepayment); only debits count, never credits. The instalments are added up for each calendar month and the month with the most is set against the declared figure. A finding is made only when the instalments exceed the declared figure by more than 10 % of their total (at least INR 1.00); a declared figure above the instalments is never reported. It is an inconsistency for the reviewer, cites the declared figure and each debit with its narration (the first six, then a count), prints its tolerance, and becomes a possible extraction error to verify when the figure or the page is doubtful. When the declared figure, an amount, a date or a narration cannot be read, or the page is of poor quality, the comparison is reported as a limitation and never as a pass. One statement is compared at a time. Measured on 44 cases of one generator (ext-dev: an application and a statement each, half digital and half mild scans, half in layout A and half in layout B; eval/emi/ext-dev.md): the 28 cases with nothing to find gave no finding; of the 12 cases whose declared figure left out a planted instalment, the 6 in layout A were found, each with the instalments' total named correctly, and the 6 in layout B were missed, because layout B heads the narration column 'Narration', a wording the statement reader does not list (on purpose: layout B is the test of unseen wording), so no narration is read there; in all 22 layout-B cases the dossier says that the narration could not be read and that any instalment among the debits was not compared. 4 cases whose instalment is narrated with a lender's name alone were not found (0 of 4), as expected. The first run of this pack (eval/emi/ext-dev.first-run.md) found the same 6 and said nothing about the 6 it missed; that statement was added after the result was seen, so the second run does not measure the check's reading independently of the fix. These figures are by construction: the same author wrote the pack and the check, and the instalments are narrated in the wordings the check reads. They say nothing about how often a real instalment is narrated like that or about other layouts and producers, and the held-out ext-test split was not run on it. Not built: instalments under a lender's name alone, instalments split over two statements added together.

capabilities.name: Context rules (income, obligations, date windows)
capabilities.note: Two rules: monthly obligations (existing instalments plus the new loan over its tenure) as a share of declared income, and a document dated more than 90 days before the application. Both are observations for the reviewer, never conflicts. Their reference limits are synthetic values chosen for this prototype, not a lending standard, and the instalment sum ignores interest. Rules taken from a lender's own policy are not built. Not measured by the evaluation: the generator holds each applicant's obligations to 40 % of income, so the obligations rule has nothing to say about a genuine case (eval/test.md).

capabilities.name: Relationships between findings (clusters)
capabilities.note: Findings are grouped when they cite the same extracted field, lie on the same place of a page (half of the smaller box inside the other), or concern the same name, address, employer or account number in different documents. A group is ranked by how many independent kinds of check fired in it (visual, arithmetic, cross-document, metadata): a count, not a probability. A group with two or more kinds gets a headline finding, classed as potential manipulation, that lists its members and cites each of their places once. Context rules are linked but count as no kind, and limitations are never grouped. Findings that share none of these stay apart even where a person would relate them. The evaluation scores findings, not groups, so grouping has no measured accuracy of its own; the overlap limit is a starting value.

capabilities.name: Entity relationship view: names, addresses, employers and account numbers across documents, and the findings that touch them
capabilities.note: Every name, address, employer and account number the extraction read goes into one list of entities, numbered in the order the documents mention them. Two writings share an entity only when the cross-document checks grade them as the same or as the same apart from form (case, spacing, punctuation, the order of the words of a name, titles, initials, an employer's legal form, the visible end of a masked account number), and a writing joins an entity only if it grades so against every writing in it; a writing those checks grade as a Minor mismatch or a Mismatch against one of them is an entity of its own, so a changed name appears as two entities and the finding that reports it touches both. An entity lists each place it is written (document, page, box, the confidence of the reading). A finding touches an entity when it cites a field that holds it or lies over its box; the headline of a group of findings and limitations are left out. The Relationships tab draws documents, entities and findings as boxes joined by lines, and the dossier lists the entities under contextual analysis. Partial: the rules are fixed and sit on the grading of the cross-document checks, with the limits stated there; this is not a trained graph model, it finds no aliases, nicknames or links by meaning, it covers these four kinds of value only, and its accuracy was not measured because the evaluation scores findings, not entities (limitation 37). Nothing in it says what a difference means.

capabilities.name: Plain-language explanations and next steps from fixed templates
capabilities.note: Fixed wording per detector and class. Without --llm nothing is written by a model; the next row covers the optional model.

capabilities.name: Explanation wording from a local language model
capabilities.note: Optional, and off unless a run is started with --llm. A small model (phi4-mini 3.8B, MIT) runs through Ollama on this computer, and the client refuses any other host. It words the headline of each group of findings and reads the case once for relations between findings, a short summary and a reading order. In these calls it sees structured findings (ids, kinds of check, titles, the values the checks used) and no page text, and it cannot add, change or remove a finding. The same flag also lets a model read the text of pages of an unsupported type, in separate calls described in the template-free row. Each part of what it writes is used only if the guard accepts it (ids, figures, dates, verdict words), and a relation only if its kind is true of what the two findings cite; the rest is dropped and logged. It is labelled as inference. Partial because it was measured only on development-set prompts, CPU only, one run each (the guard accepted 18 of 24 headline wordings), the guard does not check meaning, and nothing was run on a held-out set.

capabilities.name: Evidence traceability: finding to file, sha256, page and box, with a marked crop
capabilities.note: Every piece of evidence names its document, page and box; the trace command prints them and checks the stored file's hash.

capabilities.name: Investigation dossier: HTML (self-contained) and JSON, with its own hash
capabilities.note: Observations, inconsistencies, potential-manipulation candidates and limitations are kept in separate places. The entities the documents write about (names, addresses, employers, account numbers), each with the places it is written and the findings that touch it, are listed under contextual analysis.

capabilities.name: Dossier export as PDF
capabilities.note: Print the HTML dossier to PDF from a browser meanwhile.

capabilities.name: Tamper-evident audit trail with a verify command
capabilities.note: Each event carries the hash of the one before it, so an event edited or removed in the middle is found. The dossier records the trail's length and last hash. The chain alone does not see an event changed together with every hash after it, or a trail cut at the end: the signed checkpoints row covers that.

capabilities.name: Signed checkpoints of the audit trail
capabilities.note: At the end of a run and around the building of its dossier, the trail's length and last hash are signed with an Ed25519 key and added as one line to checkpoints.jsonl in the case folder (the trail itself gets no new event). A reviewer action after that adds a checkpoint to the chain the run began; only a run begins one. The key is made once per data folder, in its signing folder, outside the case folders. verify-audit checks every checkpoint against the trail: an event changed together with a new chain, or a trail cut at the end, no longer matches a checkpoint signed before it, and events after the last checkpoint are counted as not covered. Nothing is signed on top of a trail whose chain fails, of checkpoints that no longer hold against the trail (rewritten, cut, badly signed, a line that is not a checkpoint), or with a key that is not the one that signed them, and a signing that fails does not stop the run: it is written to the trail as an event, without a file path. What a checkpoint does not show is who held the key or when: the private key is a plain file without a password, no outside party stamps the time, and whoever can read the data folder can change the trail and sign it again with a key of their own, which only a public key the reader knows from elsewhere (verify-audit --pubkey) tells apart. The checkpoints are not linked to each other either: the last ones can be deleted together with the events they cover, and the events after the last checkpoint can be replaced; the next action signs what is left. It is a check of integrity that a reader can repeat, not a certification.

capabilities.name: Feedback from reviewer decisions to the detectors: export and counts
capabilities.note: Half of a feedback loop. What a person decided about each finding (the last status and the last note set) is read from the audit trail, after the trail's hash chain and its signed checkpoints check out, and written as JSON lines, one row per finding, with the detector, the class and the number of actions (the decisions command, and the Dossier tab of the review desk). The same rows are counted per detector and class, by status. A case whose trail does not verify, or does not agree with its checkpoints, is refused, never read as having no decisions. The other half is not built: nothing is learned from the decisions, and no threshold or detector changes because of them; a person reads the counts and edits the thresholds file. A dismissal is one person's judgement, not proof that a finding was wrong, and the counts cover whatever was reviewed, by whoever reviewed it, so they are not accuracy figures.

capabilities.name: Safe failure: rejected files, failed or stuck steps become visible limitations
capabilities.note: A step that fails or times out is listed as a limitation and the case goes on. A step stuck in native code is abandoned, not killed.

capabilities.name: Offline operation
capabilities.note: The OCR models ship inside the package. The test suite runs with connections to public addresses blocked.

capabilities.name: Review interface in the browser
capabilities.note: Runs on this computer only. Upload, a background run with progress, page images with word, field and finding boxes, evidence crops, reviewer actions written to the audit trail, the audit trail, this list and the dossier download. The server side is tested. Two automated tests drive the page in a real browser (headless Edge or Chrome, whichever is on the computer; they are skipped where there is none). The first opens a finished case, opens each of the seven tabs, waits for the words each tab must show, and fails on an uncaught page error, a console error or a request the content-security policy blocks. The second opens one finding by its address, checks that the page image and the evidence crop load and that the evidence can be marked on the page, makes a reviewer decision with the buttons and reads it back from the audit trail. They do not upload through the page, click a box on the page image, use the keyboard or judge how the page looks, and they run in one browser; the page was not tried in Firefox or Safari. Those parts were checked by hand, not by a test. Findings that share evidence are grouped in the Clusters tab, each group under its headline. The Relationships tab shows the entities the documents write about and the findings that touch them (see the entity relationship row); its page script was checked by hand in a browser, with keyboard use, and the automated test draws the tab. The Audit trail tab also says whether the trail is signed (see the signed checkpoints row); that line was checked by hand in a browser too, for a signed, an unsigned and a case whose checkpoint does not match; the automated test sees only the signed case.

capabilities.name: Handwriting and multilingual OCR
capabilities.note: Not built; text is read as printed English.

capabilities.name: Real-world document layouts at scale
capabilities.note: Only synthetic documents were used. Nothing is claimed about real ones. The held-out layout B, drawn after the specs were final, was read much worse than layout A (no id, and 34 % of the text values on digital pages).

capabilities.name: Logo and stamp comparison across documents of one issuer
capabilities.note: The logo (right of the issuer's name) and the stamp (above its caption) on each document whose type spec lists them (bank statement, loan application) are cut out, straightened by the page's turn if it is a scan, and compared by shape with those on every other document whose issuer line reads alike; a stamp is compared at its best turn within 8 degrees. A pair that differs by more than the stated limit is an inconsistency with both marks marked; every pair compared is written to the audit trail. A mark that cannot be found or read (no ink, no caption, a poor page, printed matter in the window) is a limitation, never a pass. Built and measured on synthetic marks only: six invented designs, two of which (the same motif in a circle and in an octagon) are not told apart, and a small change to a logo is not found. Held-out (eval/test.md): another logo or stamp on one document (C5) was found in 6 of 8 cases (large logo 2 of 2, large stamp 2 of 2, small stamp 2 of 2, small logo 0 of 2), and the check raised no finding on a genuine document. The held-out documents use the same six designs as the development ones.

capabilities.name: Verdicts on authenticity or intent; telling who signed; photographs and identity documents
capabilities.note: Unsupported by design. The tool lists anomalies for a human reviewer and never concludes. Signatures, logos and stamps are compared by shape between documents, which does not say who signed or who issued them. Photographs and identity documents are not examined.

limitations: Every document used to build and test this tool is synthetic. Nothing was evaluated on real documents, real scanners or real layouts.
Findings are for a human reviewer. An ordinary cause (a re-issue, a rounding rule, a misread digit, an unusual layout) can produce any of them, and the tool cannot tell which.
OCR output is a reading, not ground truth. On scans a number from a degraded or poor page is not trusted, and a conflict that rests on one is shown as a possible extraction error.

The statement checks assume the oldest row comes first and that a balance follows each row. A statement listed newest first, or with signed amounts, is reported as a layout the checks do not assume and is not checked.
A totals row at the foot of a statement is not read, so it is not checked.
A transaction row that extraction misses (for example one with a garbled date on a scan) shows up as a balance break at the next row.

The saved-revision comparison reads incremental saves only. By default a linearized PDF is not compared, at most 16 revisions of a file are opened and a page of more than 5000 words is not compared; each of these is reported as a limitation.
A PDF that was saved more than once for an ordinary reason (a correction, a re-issue, a form being filled in) shows revision observations too.

The cover check looks at opaque rectangular fills, and at pictures smaller than half a page, drawn after the text they lie over. A cover of another form (a curve, a clipped path), text hidden by its colour, and the draw order of a picture on a file whose page content is unusual are not handled; a page that draws more than 5000 objects is not examined and the dossier says so. Invisible text on a page that is mostly one picture is taken as the text layer of a scan and is not reported.

The font check compares figures and dates that stand in a text run of their own with the others in their column (four or more) or on their line (three or more). A figure inside a longer run of text is not compared, and bold against regular of one family is not. A logo, stamp or signature placed as a picture on a text page is reported like any other picture.

The metadata check reads what the file says about itself: producer and creator names, creation and modification dates. Anyone who can write the file can write them, and a file saved again for an ordinary reason shows a later modification date.

The grain check compares each scanned word with the median of its page, on the paper inside the word's box and away from the ink, and leaves out paper brighter than 250 (the scanner cuts it at white). Scanners and JPEG saves change grain for ordinary reasons. On a mildly degraded scan a changed word can keep a grain close to the page's, because the second JPEG save puts back grain of about the same size, so the check finds a patch more easily on coarser scans. Pages of poor quality are not analysed and the dossier says so.

The placement check straightens a scanned page by the turn that makes its text rows sharpest, then compares each word's position with its row, and a figure's right edge and height with the page's other figures and its column. The height of a text word is not compared (its box depends on its letters and on the slant of its line). A difference counts when it is more than 6 px (position in the row) or 10 px (figure height, right edge): four times a spread that is never taken below 1.5, 2.5 and 2.5 px. Those floors come from the largest differences on 42 genuine simulated statements (3.3, 7.0 and 6.1 px on pages not degraded), and the largest right-edge difference rose from 5.6 to 6.1 px between the first six and the next eight, so a genuine statement can still give an observation, and a shift under the limits, or a row pasted from a scan turned the same way, is not seen. On a degraded page the floors are raised by half and figure columns are rarely found (one to five figures read), so the right-edge comparison is in practice not made there. A word on a line of fewer than four words (a label and its value in a header) has no row to be measured against, so a paste there is seen only when a grain, arithmetic or cross-document check disagrees. A creased or curled page moves words and can give an observation. A page of poor quality, one with fewer than 12 words or no row of four words, or one turned by more than 2.9 degrees is not compared and the dossier says so. The turn is looked for up to 10 degrees either way; a page turned further than that is not recognised as turned and may be compared as if it were turned less, except a page that stands on its side (limitation 36).

A revision boundary is recognised from a startxref pointer followed by %%EOF. A file crafted to carry a convincing pointer inside a content stream can mislead it, which gives a false observation or a visible limitation, not a silent pass.

A document the tool does not recognise as one of the three supported types is left out of the comparisons across documents, and the dossier says which comparisons were not made. Wording unlike the specs' can read as unrecognised.

Names, addresses and employers are graded, not only passed or flagged: the same value apart from case, spacing and punctuation passes; the same words in another order, with other titles or with initials (names), the same comma-separated parts of an address in another order, or an employer with another legal form, are an observation 'written differently'; text at or above the similarity limit (0.85 for names, 0.8 for addresses and employers) that is still not identical is a 'Minor mismatch'; anything further apart is a 'Mismatch'. A name with a word left out (a middle name) is a Minor mismatch. The limits are starting values and were not tuned. In the held-out run 6 of the 7 planted changes of a name, address or employer were found; the miss is a major address change on a 120 dpi scan (eval/test.md).

An initial stands for any name it starts, so 'M. Varghese' and 'Mohan Varghese' are reported only as written differently. An address with the same words in another order but without commas is a Minor mismatch or a Mismatch by how far apart the text is, never a difference in form; any change in the numbers of an address, or in their order, is a Mismatch. An employer with a word more or fewer apart from Pvt, Ltd and the like is a Minor mismatch at a text similarity of 0.8 or more and a Mismatch below it.

Amounts are not graded: a net pay that differs from the credit by no more than the larger of INR 1 and 0.5% of the larger amount, a declared income within 5% of the gross earnings, and a sum within a document that is off by INR 1 or less pass without a finding.

On a scan a Minor mismatch of a name or an address can be one letter misread by the OCR. On a page of good quality it is shown as a conflict with a note saying so; on a degraded or poor page it is shown as a possible extraction error to verify. Account numbers have no minor grade: they match, or they are a Mismatch.
That the employer pays the salary is judged by one word of the employer's name against the descriptions of salary credits on the statement. It is a heuristic and can be wrong in either direction.
An account number that is masked, or short, matches another by its visible end, which must be at least three characters.
A payslip dated outside every statement period submitted is reported as not compared, not as a conflict. A set of several months' statements looks the same.
The same software producing different kinds of document within ten minutes is noted, and it also happens for ordinary reasons (one office system issuing both).

The context rules use reference limits that are synthetic and illustrative (obligations up to half of declared income, documents up to 90 days old); they are not a lending standard, and the instalment sum ignores interest.

Thresholds were set and checked on a development set of synthetic documents (80 cases from one generator). The test split was run once, afterwards, on the frozen tree, and nothing was tuned to its results: 79 of 96 changes were found and 1 of 144 genuine documents was flagged (eval/test.md, which also names the one fix made after a first look at layout B). Those are the figures of the tool at spec-freeze plus two fixes; the five features added after that are not covered (README, Evaluation). On other scanners, papers or layouts they may not hold; every finding prints the tolerance it used.
Untrusted files are opened in the same process as the tool. Size, page and time limits apply, but there is no sandbox.
Handwriting is not analysed, and text other than printed English is not read.

The signature comparison was fitted on synthetic signatures only, drawn by the generator for 14 invented people, and its limit was set from them. It looks in a fixed area above the caption printed under the signature, sized by the caption's text, so a layout that signs elsewhere is reported as not compared or compares the wrong marks; a stamp or a ruled line in that area counts as part of the signature unless it fills the area or reaches its edge, which is reported as not compared. A speck of ink under 12 px² is dropped, and so is a small separate piece (under a tenth of the largest) that sticks out of the box of the larger pieces; a stray larger than that, or one inside the box of the signature, counts as part of it, and in a scan of 120 dpi the drop can take off the end of a thin real stroke. A scan turned by more than 2.9 degrees is not compared. It reads shape, not authorship: one person's signatures vary from signing to signing, a scan or another kind of pen changes the strokes, and a signature copied onto another document passes. A mismatch is a lead for a reviewer and nothing more.

Findings are linked only through a shared field, an overlapping place on a page, or the same name, address, employer or account value. Two unrelated findings that share a place are grouped, and a large shape drawn over several fields can join the findings on all of them, so a group can be wider than the story behind it. Findings that a person would relate by meaning but that share none of these are not linked. A group of two kinds of check can have an ordinary cause, and its review priority is a count of kinds of check, not a likelihood. The overlap limit (half of the smaller box) is a starting value that was not tuned, and the evaluation scores findings, not groups, so it has no measured accuracy.

In the explanation calls a language model, if one is given, only words the headline of a group of findings and reads the case once for relations between findings, a short summary and a reading order; there it does not detect, read the pages or change, add or remove a finding (its separate job of reading pages of an unsupported type is the limitation on template-free reading, further down this list). The prompt carries finding titles and field values, which come from the documents, so a document can put its own text in front of the model; the guard, the fixed JSON shape and the label are what limit it. The guard checks ids, figures, dates and verdict words, not meaning, and a number written in words is not checked. Accepted wording was seen wrong: a headline that called the revision text-change finding F-001 'the debit amount of 723.26' (end-to-end run), an amount in words given as another figure, '$' written for rupees, a revision change called 'the transactions listed'. A relation's free-text reason can name the wrong document or field though its kind is checked. Measured on development-set prompts only, CPU only, one run each, a small sample: of 24 headline wordings the guard accepted 18 from phi4-mini and 13 from qwen3-4b-instruct; reading a case, 9 of 26 relations were kept from phi4-mini (5 readings) and 19 of 23 from qwen3 (10 readings). A call took 17 to 26 s on average for a headline and 40 to 48 s for a reading (the longest 112 s), and the model is loaded for every call, so a case with a model takes a minute or more, and free RAM fell to about 2 GiB. A reply is cut at 1024 tokens, and phi4-mini was seen to write on without end in 2 of 16 readings before the reply format bounded its lists. Not measured: GPU use, a vision-language model on page images, and any model on the held-out split.

The logo and stamp comparison was fitted on synthetic marks only: six invented designs of each, drawn by the generator, with both limits set from them. Two of the six logos, which share a motif and differ only in the outline, are not told apart at any limit; a small change to a logo (one point moved a tenth of its width) is not found; and the margin at the logo limit is narrow (the largest genuine pair is 6.5 against a limit of 10.5, the nearest pair of designs that can be told apart 13.8). It looks in a fixed window right of the line that names the issuer (the topmost line of page 1 that reads as a name among those within 15 % of the tallest) and above the caption printed under the stamp, sized by the text beside it, so a layout that puts a mark elsewhere is reported as not compared or compares the wrong ink; a window that is mostly ink or has ink at its edge is reported as not compared. The same two drops of ink apply as for signatures. Under a short issuer name the line beneath it runs on into the logo window: its words are erased from the window, and where that line stops inside the logo (or text is printed over the logo itself) the logo is reported as not compared, because the two documents would cut it differently. Documents count as one issuer when that line reads alike (80 % likeness), so a misread or changed name leaves a document ungrouped and unchecked, and a title more than 15 % taller than the issuer's name, printed alike on the documents of two issuers, takes the place of the name and groups them, so their different marks are reported as a difference. When two documents carry a mark but no two share an issuer line, that is one limitation; a single marked document says nothing. A scan turned by more than 2.9 degrees is not compared, and the round stamp of a payslip is not compared. It reads shape, not origin: a mark copied from another document passes.

A scanned page is classed good, degraded or poor by its sharpness alone, with two limits set on the simulated scans of one generator. A page from another scanner or with other content can fall on the other side of a limit: a blurred page called good has its digits trusted, a sharp one called degraded has its conflicts shown as limitations to verify. Real scanners are not simulated.

The OCR can misread a letter or a digit with no sign of doubt. The tool does not repair what it reads, and a value read from a page classed good carries the confidence of that class (up to 0.95), so a wrong one is not marked as doubtful. The evaluation counts these in its 'wrong, trusted' column: in the held-out run 16 text values (4 and 4 on layout A, mild and 150 dpi; 3 and 5 on layout B) and no amount, date or id.

Extraction depends on the wordings of labels, column headings and captions that the spec of each document type lists. A wording that is not listed leaves its value missing, and whatever depends on that value is left unchecked; the tool says so as a limitation and does not guess. On the held-out layout B, about half of whose wordings the specs do not list, digital pages gave 91 % of amounts, 97 % of dates, 34 % of text values and no id, and the checks within a document could not be made in full on any of its 24 genuine statements and 24 genuine payslips (eval/test.md). A document that words its labels differently from the specs will meet the same limit, and a value under a label that is not listed cannot be compared with another document's.

The grain and placement checks found few changed scans. In the held-out split they found 3 of the 16 scans that were changed by pasting from another scan or by erasing and retyping (the placement check 1 of the 8 pasted scans, the grain check 2 of the 8 retyped ones), arithmetic and cross-document checks found 3 more, and 10 were not found at all; at 120 dpi 2 of 9 changes of any kind were found. A scan on which the tool raised nothing therefore says little about whether it was changed. These checks also gave the one flag on a genuine document, a 120 dpi scan (eval/test.md).

The reader does not turn a page back upright. It recognises one case, a page that stands on its side (a scan turned a quarter turn, or a PDF page stored turned 90 or 270 degrees), because most of its words are taller than wide. Such a page is read as poor quality and the dossier says why. Its values carry low confidence, and the checks that compare them, the placement of its words and its marks are not run on it. The rule was added after cases with one such page gave false conflicts: the page's rows are the document's columns, so a value pairs with the wrong label. In 4 genuine development cases of three documents (2 scans, 2 PDFs), a statement turned a quarter gave a false address conflict with the other documents and a payslip turned a quarter gave false employer and payer conflicts, in every case; with the rule, the turned page gave no flag in any of them. A page that is upside down is not recognised (the tool has no test for it). It is read, few of its fields are found (8 to 38 of the 78 to 188 of a statement in those cases), and a check can give a false result: a statement scanned upside down gave a false placement observation in 1 of the 2 scans, and a statement stored as a PDF turned half a turn gave a false account-number conflict with the other documents in both PDFs. No page in the development or the held-out split is turned, so none of this is in the reported figures. A page should be turned upright before it is submitted.

The entity view puts two writings together by the pairwise grading of the cross-document checks, which is not transitive. A writing joins the first entity, in the order the documents mention them, in which every writing is graded as the same as it or as the same apart from form, and is an entity of its own if there is none, so two writings graded as a mismatch are never in one entity. A writing that fits more than one entity sits in the first, so which entities there are, and where such a writing is put, depend on the order the documents are read in. An initial stands for any name it starts, so 'M. Varghese' fits both 'Mohan Varghese' and 'Manoj Varghese' (a Minor mismatch with each other) and sits with the one read first, and a masked account number fits any number that ends the same way. Only names, addresses, employers and account numbers are entities. Dates, amounts and ids are not, and neither are aliases, nicknames, a person named by role ('the borrower') or a name inside running text. A value the extraction missed is absent from the view, and one it misread is an entity of its own, so a letter misread in a name appears as two names. A finding touches an entity only through a field it cites or a box it lies over, so one that concerns an entity in some other way is not drawn on it, and every finding that does touch one is drawn whatever its review status. The view has no accuracy measured, because the evaluation scores findings and not entities, and it does not say that two entities are, or are not, one person or one thing.

The signed checkpoints show that the audit trail still reads as it did when a checkpoint was signed. They do not show who held the key or when: the private key is a plain file without a password in the signing folder of the data folder, the time in a checkpoint is the clock of the machine that signed it, and no outside party stamps it. Whoever can read that folder can change the trail, work the hashes out again and sign it with a key of their own; a reader tells that apart only by knowing the public key from somewhere else (verify-audit --pubkey).

A case folder whose checkpoints.jsonl was removed reads as unsigned, which verify-audit reports and passes unless a public key is given. A reviewer action does not sign such a case afresh, but the next run of it signs the trail as it stands, with the key of the data folder. The last checkpoints can also be deleted together with the events they cover; what is left still holds, and the next action signs it. Likewise the events after the last checkpoint, which are counted as not covered and not as changed, can be replaced before the next action signs them. A copy of a checkpoint or of the head that verify-audit printed, kept outside the case folder, shows the cut; only a copy of the head, taken while those events were there, shows the replacement. A checkpoint carries the public key that signed it, so without a key known beforehand it shows only that one key signed this trail.

The tool makes no claim of compliance with SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27037 or any other standard. The audit trail and its signed checkpoints are checks of integrity that a reader can repeat; a standard also asks about people, procedure and the custody of the original files, which software cannot supply.

Template-free reading by the model (--llm) is inference. The model decides which words are a fact and what to call it; code checks only that the words are on the page and that the value is inside them. The name is not checked: a bank account number was named invoice_number in the measurement. The value is the page's own text, so a letter or digit the OCR misread is copied as misread (a decimal comma read as a point gave 1.150.00) and nothing repairs it. Such a field has a confidence below the doubt limit whatever the page quality, feeds no check and no comparison across documents, and raises no finding: a page of an unsupported type is listed, not examined for inconsistencies, and the type is not the model's call.

Template-free reading was measured on one pack made for it: 7 synthetic cases of an invoice and an electricity bill in two layouts, one run per model, on the development split; the held-out ext-test split was not read by any model. Two defects of the code that reads the model were found and fixed on that data, and the figures before and after are both in docs/spike-x-extraction.md. phi4-mini (97 of 182 facts right) joined two labels and their two values into single fields on layout B, missed the tax amount of 2 of 7 invoices and the closing meter reading of all three layout B bills, and left 9 of 15 facts of a 120 dpi bill unread; qwen3-4b-instruct-2507 (38 of 156 facts right on the 6 cases it finished) put the label inside the value and gave one reply that was not JSON. Other documents, other languages, longer pages and other models are untested.

The model is shown at most the first 60 lines of each of the first 2 pages of a document, and the first 60 items of its reply are used (the prompt asks for 20, and phi4-mini gave 21 to 25 on 4 of 14 pages); what is left out is counted and said as a limitation in the dossier. A call takes 60 to 123 s a page on this CPU (mean 88 s), the model is loaded for each call, and after one failed call the rest of the case is not read by the model. It is given the text of the page only, never boxes or images.

Compression-history analysis of scanned pages was set up on the first 36 cases of one synthetic pack (payslips, one generator, one JPEG writer), so its figures are in-sample; 72 further cases of the same generator gave the same result, which shows that the figures do not depend on those 36 draws, not that they hold on other scans. Its limit for an earlier save (a dip of 1.3) lies in a gap that is empty in this pack: pages without an earlier save measure 1.015 to 1.032 (24 pages: 12 saved once, 1.015 to 1.030, and 12 saved twice at the same quality; 6 more saved once at quality 35 cannot be measured) and the 78 pages with one 1.82 or more, so a real page with a weak trace between them is not covered by any measurement. The held-out ext-test split was not run on it.

Compression-history analysis sees nothing when the page was saved once, when the last save is less than 10 quality points above the earlier one (which includes a last save at a lower quality than the earlier one, as when a mailer shrinks a good scan: invisible by design), or when the changed part has the page's own JPEG grid and quality; the project's own splice of a part of another scan of the same level is of that kind, and on the dev split a region appeared on 1 of its 5 scans (cause not examined, not claimed as a find) while on another the history was found and no region. A page whose last save is under quality 40 is not examined: the lowest quality tried is 30, so there is no earlier save to look for; the absence of a region on such a page is not a result (21 of the 90 unchanged dev scans, 2 of 12 and 4 of 24 in the pack). It found none of 18 edits whose earlier save was written with Photoshop-family quantisation tables instead of libjpeg's, so it may depend on the earlier save having been written by libjpeg; whether real scanners and programs do so is not known. The earlier quality it names is where the trace shows, in steps of 5: with earlier saves at 82, 47 and 33 it was exactly right on 0 of 16.

A compression-history observation is not a statement that anything was changed: a page put together from more than one scan, and a stamp, date, page number or sticker that the scanner or a program added later, leave the same mark. A picture that is not the saved JPEG (a PNG, a scaled or turned picture) and the rendered page of a scanned PDF (the embedded picture is not taken out) are listed as not examined, and a page read from the text layer is not examined by it.

The reused-signature check was set on the signature pairs of one synthetic pack (one generator): its limit of 5 % lies above 23 of the 24 copies and below all 47 pairs from separate signings, so the figures are in-sample. The 24th copy lies 6.7 % away (a scan at 120 dpi) and is not found; the nearest separate pair lies 8.8 % away, 3.8 points above the limit. A limit of 8 % would have found all 24 and flagged none of the 47, with 0.8 points to the nearest separate pair instead of 3.8; the limit was not moved to fit the one miss on one pack. A person who signs very much alike every time, a signature stamp, software that puts a stored image of a signature on each document, or a plain mark that is not solid (a hollow box, a diagonal stroke) printed the same on two documents will be reported; a solid bar, a dot or a block is skipped, and a dashed rule or a rule that is not quite level can fall on either side of that line. A copy that was scanned at a low resolution can fall above the limit (one of 24 did, at 120 dpi); a signature that was redrawn or traced is not reported. Stamps and logos are not compared for sameness (at the limit of its first attempt, 18 of 48 separate synthetic stamp pressings were flagged, and 27 lie within the 5 % used here, so a rule that flagged reused stamps would have flagged separate ones); whether real stamps would separate is not known. Only documents of a type with a signature caption in its spec are compared. The held-out ext-test split was not run on it.

Reviewer decisions are counted, not learned from: a dismissal is one person's judgement and is not proof that a finding was wrong, a finding nobody has acted on counts as open, and the counts cover whatever was reviewed, by whoever reviewed it, so they are not accuracy figures. No threshold or detector changes because of them; a person reads the counts and edits the thresholds file.

The raw file-structure check reads names, positions and sizes from the stored bytes. It does not check any signature's cryptography, does not open, decode or run embedded files, scripts or actions, and is not a malware scanner; a signed PDF always carries a limitation that says the signature was not verified.

Every fact the raw file-structure check reports also occurs in ordinary files (a program that pads a file or writes a trailer, saving again in place, a second signature, a countersignature or a form filled in after a signature, an attachment or an /OpenAction written by a generator, an /Info record that differs from the XMP packet, an editor used to crop a genuine photograph), and anyone who can write a file can write each of these fields. Nothing reported means only that none of these facts was found.

The figures for the raw file-structure check are by construction: 120 files from one generator, built by the author of the check with the check in view (60 untouched, 60 with one planted change). They show what the check does with the changes it was written for, are not a detection rate, and say nothing about files made by other programs.

The raw file-structure check does not look at bytes before the PDF header (such a file is turned away at upload), file-attachment annotations, text chunks stored after the image data of a PNG, or a JPEG picture inside a PDF that has another filter in front of DCT. The list of image-editor names is fixed and matched at the start of a word ('canva' also matches 'Canvas'), so a program with a similar name is named too and an editor that is not on the list is not. Pictures past the first 50 of a PDF and objects past the first 20,000 are not followed (a limitation says so). A document the read step could not open gets no byte-level check.

The learned word check compares each measurable word of a scan with the other words of its page and lists the words whose weighted score over fourteen measures reaches a limit. The score is not a probability and does not say that anything was changed: it says how much a word looks like the synthetic edits the weights were fitted to. Uneven lighting, a stamp, a fold, a second JPEG save, another typeface or size, and a field filled in by another program move the same measures.

The learned word check was fitted to edits made by this project's own generator (parts of other scans pasted in, pasted fields and blocks, the same place of another scan pasted in, retyped amounts) on scans from the project's scan simulator (JPEG, three levels of quality), and measured on held-out pages from the same generator: 16 of 36 and 59 of 72 changed pages found, none of the 195 unedited pages flagged. The generator, the edits and the check have one author, so the figures show that these edits are found, not that edits made by anyone else, on other scanners, at other resolutions or in other file formats, would be. No real scan was used. None of 195 unedited pages flagged does not exclude a rate of about 1.5 % of unedited pages flagged. Of the generator's two page layouts, the changed pages measured are those of layout A and the payslips of the compression-history pack (in both layouts); edits on statements and applications of layout B were not measured, and 72 genuine scan pages of layout B tried afterwards were not flagged, which says nothing about edited ones.

The learned word check finds some kinds of edit less often than others: on the held-out pack pages, pasted blocks 18 of 18 and pasted fields 17 of 18, but the same place of another scan pasted in (kind aligned) 12 of 18 and retyped amounts 12 of 18, which the grain and placement checks find 18 of 18. For parts of another scan pasted into a page, most of its gain over those two checks comes from two hand-written measures of how far a word sits off the line of its neighbours (alone they find 13 of 72 development pages; the other twelve measures alone find none). A change that leaves a word's grain, edges, strokes, JPEG grid and place as the page's own is not seen.

The learned word check looks only at pages read by OCR that are not of poor quality, and only at words with enough paper in their box to measure; a page with fewer than 12 measurable words is not compared, and a limitation says so for each such document. It does not look at digital PDFs. It lists at most eight words a page.

A table row is a line whose first cell has the shape the column asks for (a date, or an amount). A cell with that shape that cannot be read as one, such as the amount 57.500.00, the date O3/05/2026 or a date with a month over 12, stays a row with that cell unreadable: the statement is reported as not fully verifiable and the value is named, an amount that cannot be read leaves the stretch of the balance chain that holds it untested, and a date that cannot be read leaves that row out of the date checks. A row whose first cell has no such shape at all (letters in the date, a date split into words, a missing separator) is left out of the table, and the balance chain can then show a break that is really a row that was not read; the explanation of that finding lists this among the possible causes.

A balance printed with Dr (for example 5,000.00 Dr) is read as money owed, that is minus, and one printed with Cr as money held; the marker on a debit or credit amount only names the column and gives no sign. A statement with one Amount column and a separate column that marks each line Dr or Cr is not read: its debit and credit cells are reported missing, the balance chain is not tested and the checks say they cannot fully verify the statement (a probe of six such statements gave that limitation and no false finding). Amounts with a minus sign and no marker are the signed layout that the statement checks do not assume, stated above.

The declared-EMI check reads a debit as an instalment only when its narration holds the whole word EMI, instalment (also spelt installment, or instl) or loan, and none of the words fee, charge, penalty, GST, tax, bounce, return, refund, reversal, waiver, insurance, premium, closure, foreclosure or prepayment. An instalment paid under a lender's name alone, or written in a way these words do not cover, is not seen (none of the 4 such cases of the pack was found), and a transfer whose narration says loan, or a payment made for someone else, can be counted as an instalment. On one statement the check takes the calendar month with the most instalments, and it takes one statement at a time, so instalments split over two statements are not added together. A declared figure above the instalments is never reported, since an instalment paid from another account or in cash has an ordinary cause.

The declared-EMI check cannot read a narration when the statement reader does not list the heading of that column. The generator's layout B heads it 'Narration', which the reader leaves out on purpose (layout B is the test of wording the reader has not seen), so there every narration is empty: 6 of the 6 planted gaps in layout B were missed, and for all 22 layout-B cases of the pack the dossier said that the narration could not be read and that any instalment among the debits was not compared. A statement that heads the column with a wording the reader does not list would be treated the same way: a limitation, and no comparison.

The figures for the declared-EMI check are by construction: 44 cases from one generator, built by the author of the check with the check in view, the instalments narrated in the wordings the check reads (EMI, instalment, loan). They show what the check does with those wordings and say nothing about how often a real instalment is narrated like that, or about other layouts, other producers or another language. The statement that an unread narration was not compared was added after the first run, which had missed six cases without a word; both reports are kept, so the second run does not measure the check's reading independently of that fix. The held-out ext-test split was not run on it.

Pictures that carry no scanner grain (a page printed or rendered to an image) are not given to the grain, placement and learned-word checks, and the dossier says so for each such document. An edit on such a page is found only by the arithmetic and cross-document checks: 88 of 108 edits in a probe of 6 cases printed to 150 dpi png, 200 dpi png and 200 dpi jpg, and none of the three scan checks ever put a finding on an edit there. The line comes from simulated scans, not from a real scanner. The gate was added after that probe had shown the three checks putting an observation on 15 of 18 clean printed pages (0 of 18 after), and its line was set on the same development pages, so those figures show what the gate does with them and not how it behaves on other scanners or other pictures; no held-out split was used. A real scan that is very clean, cut at white or denoised may be taken for such a page and then goes unchecked by those three checks, with the dossier saying so.
assumptions: Dates are read day first (DD/MM/YYYY); a date that could be read another way is marked ambiguous and given a low confidence.
Amounts are in rupees, with lakh or western digit grouping.
A usable PDF text layer is taken as read; a page whose text layer is unusable is read by OCR instead.
Boxes are pixels of the page rendered at 200 dpi unless a page says otherwise; points are pixels x 72 / dpi.
Documents are synthetic or authorised for the purpose, and one case is analysed at a time on one machine.
